simplified.title: Smeden som de ikke turte slippe inn i helvete

english.title: The Blacksmith They Dared Not Let into Hell

world: Old rural Norway, long ago, when Our Lord and Saint Peter still walked the earth. The smithy is a squat, soot-blackened log building with a turf roof, a crooked stone chimney and wide double doors, beside a dusty country road through farmland. A gnarled old pear tree heavy with yellow pears grows against its sunny wall. Inside are a brick forge with a big leather bellows, an anvil on a stump, tools on the walls and, in the corner, a big, deep armchair of worn dark-red leather. The steel-wire purse is a small, round coin purse of woven silver-grey steel wire with a snap clasp. Far along the road, the way forks: one road climbs into white clouds to the tall white gate of Heaven; the other dips into a smoky, rocky gully to the gate of Hell, a tall, crooked, soot-black iron gate with nine big locks.
palette: Blazing summer heat in a dusty farming valley: glaring white-gold afternoons, parched straw-yellow fields, an ochre dust road and ripe yellow pears among dusty leaves. Inside the smithy: soot-black and charcoal lit by ember-orange glow and showers of sparks. At the end, soft white cloud and pale gold light at the gate of Heaven, and a smoky plum-purple haze at the gate of Hell.

cast.look: A tall, long-legged blacksmith of about forty with a broad barrel chest and thick, strong forearms, a long, cocky face with a jutting chin, a big bumpy nose, twinkling hazel eyes, a chestnut-brown handlebar moustache curled up at both ends and short chestnut hair that sticks straight up like a brush. He wears a collarless undyed linen shirt with rolled-up sleeves, a long scorched brown leather apron, dark-blue wool breeches, heavy black boots and a red kerchief knotted round his neck.
cast.portrait: Background: the glowing forge in his smithy.

simplified.name: Smeden
simplified.description: En sterk og selvsikker smed som har inngått kontrakt med Fanden, men bruker list og tre ønsker til å snu avtalen i sin favør.

english.name: The Blacksmith
english.description: A proud master of his trade who bargains for greatness, then relies on boldness and clever wishes to escape the Devil’s claim.

cast.look: A calm, slim traveller of about forty-five with an upright bearing, an oval face, a straight nose, warm dark-brown eyes with smile lines, short curly dark-brown hair with a few silver threads and a short, neat dark-brown beard. He wears a long, hooded slate-grey travelling cloak over a plain undyed linen tunic tied with a cord, and worn leather sandals. He looks like an ordinary, humble wanderer, with no halo.
cast.portrait: Background: the dusty country road in hot summer sunshine.

simplified.name: Vårherre
simplified.description: En vandrer som avslører en overnaturlig smikunst, gir smeden tre ønsker og kommenterer det urettferdige smeden gjør.

english.name: Our Lord
english.description: A calm wanderer who demonstrates miraculous skill in the forge, rebukes cruelty, and grants the blacksmith three ill-chosen but potent wishes.

cast.look: A tall, broad-shouldered old fisherman of about seventy with a weathered, ruddy face, a big round nose, pale blue eyes under bushy white eyebrows and a thick, curly white beard. He wears a navy-blue fisherman's cap with a short peak, a long rust-brown coat over a grey sailcloth smock, rolled-up dark trousers and sturdy boots. A big, old iron key hangs from a leather cord at his belt. No halo.

simplified.name: Sankt Peter
simplified.description: Vårherres følgesvenn, som sier at smeden ønsket som en tosk og heller burde ha bedt om Guds nåde, og som til slutt gløtter på himmelporten.

english.name: Saint Peter
english.description: The Lord’s companion who warns that the blacksmith should have wished for grace instead of tricks, and who guards Heaven’s gate at the end.

cast.look: A short, pot-bellied devil no taller than a boy of ten, with shiny tomato-red skin, a round face with a button nose, big goggly amber eyes, pointy ears, a long, pointed black goatee and two big black ram's horns curling out of his forehead. He has a very long, thin tail with an arrow-shaped tip and little black goat hooves, and wears a smart soot-black waistcoat with shiny brass buttons stretched over his belly. Vain, boastful and silly rather than frightening.
cast.portrait: Background: the pear tree full of yellow pears.

simplified.name: Fanden
simplified.description: Djevelen som kommer for å hente smeden etter kontrakten, men blir fanget i pæretreet, lenestolen og til slutt i ståltrådpungen.

english.name: The Devil
english.description: A contract-bound tempter repeatedly humiliated by the blacksmith’s traps: the pear tree, the armchair, and the steel-wire purse.

cast.look: A thin, narrow-shouldered young journeyman tailor of about nineteen with a narrow pale face, a long pointed nose, big anxious grey eyes and neat, slicked-down black hair with a straight side parting. He wears a snug plum-purple waistcoat with a row of tiny silver buttons over a white shirt, grey knee breeches, white stockings and black buckle shoes, with a yellow tape measure round his neck and a red pincushion on his wrist, and carries a heavy black pressing iron.
cast.portrait: Background: the fork in the dusty road.

simplified.name: Skreddersvennen
simplified.description: En tynn skreddersvenn med pressejernet i hånda, som smeden tar igjen ved korsveien, og som skal prøve å slippe inn i himmerike.

english.name: The Journeyman Tailor
english.description: A thin traveler bound for Heaven, whose timely entrance contrasts the blacksmith’s late, forceful attempt to follow.

places.name: the Smithy
places.look: The inside of a small, sooty log smithy with a low beamed ceiling: a brick forge with a hood and glowing coals, a big leather bellows beside it, a black anvil on a thick tree stump in the middle, hammers, tongs and horseshoes hanging on the dark log walls, a wooden water barrel, and in the corner a big, deep armchair of worn dark-red leather. Wide double doors open onto bright sunshine and the dusty road.

places.name: the Smithy Yard
places.look: Outside the smithy: a squat, soot-blackened log building with a grass-covered turf roof, a crooked stone chimney and wide double doors, beside a dusty ochre country road with dry grassy verges. A gnarled old pear tree heavy with ripe yellow pears grows against its sunny side wall, with a split-rail fence, parched hay meadows and a few birches beyond.

cover.prompt: Inside the Smithy, lit by the orange glow of the forge, the Blacksmith stands at his anvil with a nail held in his tongs and his big sledgehammer resting on his shoulder, glancing towards the door with a sly, twinkling grin. Round the edge of the open door, the Devil pokes his head in, nose first, with an eager grin, his long tail curling up behind him in the golden summer light.

simplified.caption: Smeden og Fanden, som har kommet for å hente ham.
simplified.alt: Smeden står ved ambolten med slegga på skulderen og smiler lurt. Rundt dørkarmen stikker en liten, rød djevel inn hodet.

english.caption: The blacksmith, and the Devil who has come to fetch him.
english.alt: The blacksmith stands at his anvil with his sledgehammer on his shoulder, grinning slyly. Round the door frame, a small red devil pokes his head in.

illustrations.prompt: In the Smithy Yard, in front of the wide double doors, Our Lord straightens up beside a brown horse that now stands on four shining new shoes, and pats its neck as the last wisps of coal smoke drift out of the doorway. The horse's owner, a stocky farmer in a straw hat, beams. By the open door, the Blacksmith stares, speechless, a hammer hanging forgotten in his hand, and Saint Peter smiles faintly behind him.

simplified.caption: «Du er ikke så dårlig smed, du», sa smeden.
simplified.alt: Vårherre klapper en brun hest som står på fire blanke, nye hestesko. Bonden som eier hesten, smiler fornøyd, og smeden står i smiedøra og måper.

english.anchor: The blacksmith stood by the open door and watched.
english.caption: For once in his life he had nothing to say.
english.alt: Our Lord pats a brown horse that stands on four shining new shoes. The horse's owner beams, and the blacksmith stands in the forge doorway, speechless.

illustrations.prompt: In the orange glow of the forge in the Smithy, a lovely young girl with rosy cheeks and fair braids stands up straight where the Blacksmith's bent old mother was a moment ago, still in the old woman's long brown dress, white headscarf and black shawl, and gazes at her smooth young hands in wonder. Our Lord stands calmly beside the forge as sparks drift in the air. The Blacksmith watches from the door with his arms folded, and two young apprentices goggle against the wall.

simplified.anchor: Han tok et fast tak i den gamle kona og løftet henne inn mot essa.
simplified.caption: Av den gamle kona smidde Vårherre ei ung og vakker jente.
simplified.alt: I gløden fra essa står ei ung, rødkinnet jente i den gamle konas klær og ser forundret på hendene sine. Vårherre står rolig ved siden av, og smeden står i døra med armene i kors.

english.anchor: He took hold of the old woman, laid her in the forge
english.caption: Out of her he forged a lovely young girl.
english.alt: In the glow of the forge stands a rosy young girl in the old woman's clothes, gazing at her hands in wonder. Our Lord stands calmly beside her, and the blacksmith watches from the door with his arms folded.

illustrations.prompt: In the Smithy Yard, thick black smoke pours out of the chimney and the open double doors. The Blacksmith, red-faced and sulky, counts silver coins one by one into the outstretched palm of the horse's owner, a tall, stern man in a long riding coat and a broad-brimmed hat, who glares down at him. Two soot-faced apprentices cough in the doorway behind them. Hot, hazy afternoon light.

simplified.anchor: Men det gikk som en kunne vente.
simplified.caption: Smeden måtte betale for hesten.
simplified.alt: Svart røyk velter ut av smia. Smeden teller surt sølvmynter over i hånda til en høy, sint mann med bredbremmet hatt.

english.anchor: But it went the way you might expect.
english.caption: The blacksmith had to pay for the horse.
english.alt: Black smoke pours out of the forge. The blacksmith sulkily counts silver coins into the hand of a tall, angry man in a broad-brimmed hat.

illustrations.prompt: In the wide doorway of the Smithy, the Blacksmith proudly holds up a small, round steel-wire purse in one hand and points with the other out at the old pear tree by the wall, heavy with yellow pears; behind him in the corner stands the big, worn dark-red leather armchair. Our Lord listens with a patient smile, and Saint Peter, beside him, frowns and shakes his head.

simplified.anchor: «Du ønsket som en tosk», sa Sankt Peter.
simplified.caption: «Du ønsket som en tosk», sa Sankt Peter.
simplified.alt: Smeden holder stolt opp en liten pengepung av ståltråd og peker ut mot pæretreet. Inne i smia står en stor lenestol. Vårherre smiler, og Sankt Peter rister på hodet.

english.anchor: “You wished like a fool,” said Saint Peter.
english.caption: “You wished like a fool,” said Saint Peter.
english.alt: The blacksmith proudly holds up a little steel-wire purse and points out at the pear tree. A big armchair stands inside the forge. Our Lord smiles, and Saint Peter shakes his head.

illustrations.prompt: In the Smithy Yard in the golden evening sun, the Devil sits stuck high up in the old pear tree, one arm still stretched out towards the biggest yellow pear, his tail tangled round a branch and his face frozen in dismay: he can neither climb up nor down. Below on the grass, the Blacksmith looks up at him with a sly little smile. Seen from low down, looking up into the tree.

simplified.anchor: Fanden takket for tilbudet og klatret opp.
simplified.caption: Han kom verken opp eller ned.
simplified.alt: Fanden sitter fast oppe i pæretreet og strekker seg etter den største pæra. Nede på bakken står smeden og smiler lurt.

english.anchor: The Devil thanked him kindly and climbed up.
english.caption: He couldn’t climb up and he couldn’t climb down.
english.alt: The Devil sits stuck high in the pear tree, reaching for the biggest pear. Below, the blacksmith looks up with a sly smile.

illustrations.prompt: Inside the Smithy, the Devil is stuck fast in the big, worn dark-red leather armchair in the corner, straining to get up, his face purple with rage, shaking his fist and lashing his tail. At the anvil, the Blacksmith spreads his hands apologetically and nods at an iron nail held in his tongs, as if to say it is all the iron's fault. The forge glows orange behind them.

simplified.anchor: Fanden ba først pent om å få reise seg.
simplified.caption: Fanden ba først pent om å få reise seg. Så ble han sint og begynte å true.
simplified.alt: Fanden sitter fast i lenestolen og rister rasende på neven. Smeden sprer hendene unnskyldende ut og nikker mot spikeren i tanga.

english.anchor: At first the Devil asked nicely to be let out of the chair.
english.caption: Then he lost his temper and started making threats.
english.alt: The Devil sits stuck in the armchair, shaking his fist in fury. The blacksmith spreads his hands apologetically and nods at the nail in his tongs.

illustrations.prompt: Close-up at the anvil in the Smithy: the Blacksmith holds the little round steel-wire purse wide open in his big, calloused hands with an innocent face. The Devil, who has made himself as small as a mouse, is climbing into it head first among the silver coins, with only his little hooves and his long, thin tail still sticking out. Warm orange forge light.

simplified.caption: Han gjorde seg liten og krøp inn i pungen.
simplified.alt: Smeden holder en liten pengepung av ståltråd åpen i hånda. Fanden er blitt bitte liten og kryper inn, så bare beina og halen stikker ut.

english.caption: He made himself small and crawled in among the coins.
english.alt: The blacksmith holds a little steel-wire purse open in his hand. The Devil, now tiny, is crawling inside, with only his hooves and tail sticking out.

illustrations.prompt: Wide view of the Smithy Yard on a bright day: the Devil, back to his full size, races away down the dusty road as fast as his legs will go, his tail streaming out behind him and dust flying from his hooves, not daring to look back. In the wide doorway stands the Blacksmith, leaning on his big sledgehammer and holding up the open, soot-blackened purse with a broad grin.

simplified.anchor: Han åpnet pungen, og Fanden for av sted så fort at han ikke turte se
simplified.caption: Fanden for av sted så fort at han ikke turte se seg tilbake en gang.
simplified.alt: Fanden løper av sted bortover den støvete veien med halen flagrende bak seg. I døra til smia står smeden med slegga og den åpne pungen.

english.anchor: He opened the purse, and the Devil shot off so fast he didn’t even dare
english.caption: The Devil shot off so fast he didn’t even dare look back.
english.alt: The Devil races off down the dusty road with his tail streaming behind him. In the forge doorway stands the blacksmith with his sledgehammer and the open purse.

illustrations.prompt: Wide view of a long, dusty road in late-afternoon light, at the crossroads where it forks. The Blacksmith, his big sledgehammer over his shoulder, has caught up with the Journeyman Tailor, who scurries along clutching his heavy pressing iron. Beyond them the two roads part: one climbs a green hill into soft white clouds towards a tall white gate far away; the other winds down into a smoky, rocky gully towards a dark iron gate.

simplified.anchor: Da han hadde gått et godt stykke, kom han til korsveien
simplified.caption: Ved korsveien tok han igjen en skreddersvenn med pressejernet i hånda.
simplified.alt: Smeden med slegga på skulderen og en tynn skreddersvenn med pressejern står der veien deler seg. Den ene veien går opp mot skyene, den andre ned i en røykfylt kløft.

english.anchor: When he had walked a good long way
english.caption: At the crossroads he caught up with a journeyman tailor.
english.alt: The blacksmith, with his sledgehammer on his shoulder, and a thin journeyman tailor with a pressing iron stand where the road forks. One road climbs into the clouds, the other dips into a smoky gully.

illustrations.prompt: At the bottom of a smoky, rocky gully, the Blacksmith stands before the tall, crooked, soot-black gate of Hell with his sledgehammer on his shoulder, eyebrows raised, as nine big iron locks snap shut one after another down the middle of the gate and a huge padlock swings on the bolt. Plum-purple smoke curls over the top of the gate. Seen from just behind the Blacksmith's shoulder.

simplified.anchor: Smeden sto utenfor og hørte det klirre og smelle, lås etter lås.
simplified.caption: Smeden hørte det klirre og smelle, lås etter lås.
simplified.alt: Smeden står foran en høy, svart jernport i en røykfylt kløft. Ni store låser har smelt igjen nedover porten, og en diger hengelås henger på slåen.

english.anchor: Outside, the blacksmith heard the bolts shoot home, one after another.
english.caption: Outside, the blacksmith heard the bolts shoot home, one after another.
english.alt: The blacksmith stands before a tall, black iron gate in a smoky gully. Nine big locks have snapped shut down the gate, and a huge padlock hangs on the bolt.

illustrations.prompt: High up among soft white clouds, Saint Peter holds the tall white gate of Heaven open just a crack, and the thin Journeyman Tailor slips in sideways with his pressing iron as a stripe of golden light spills out through the gap. At that very moment the Blacksmith's big sledgehammer sails through the gap in a high arc, well over their heads. Six or seven steps behind, the Blacksmith leans forward with his arm still stretched out from the throw.

simplified.anchor: «Her er det nok best å skynde seg», tenkte han.
simplified.caption: Han kastet slegga inn gjennom glipa i samme stund som skredderen smatt inn.
simplified.alt: Sankt Peter holder himmelporten på gløtt, og skreddersvennen smetter inn. Over hodene deres flyr smedens slegge inn gjennom glipa, mens smeden står noen skritt bak.

english.caption: He hurled his sledgehammer through the gap just as the tailor slipped in.
english.alt: Saint Peter holds Heaven's gate open a crack, and the tailor slips inside. Over their heads, the blacksmith's sledgehammer sails through the gap, while the blacksmith stands a few steps behind.
